title: Embedding width contract evolution and client handshake protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Several customers and internal reranking pipelines require a change to the canonical embedding vector dimensionality (width). Changing the width impacts stored indexes, inference latency, client SDKs, and downstream rerankers. We need a prescriptive, low-risk protocol for evolving the embedding contract (increase or decrease dims) that minimizes customer downtime, bounds unit-cost regressions, and provides clear client compatibility behavior.

Goal: Define and implement a "soft-contract" evolution and client handshake protocol that: (1) lets us serve multiple coexisting embedding widths; (2) supports non-disruptive online reindex with priority and backfill scheduling; (3) surfaces clear SDK-level negotiation and transparent error modes for clients; and (4) provides telemetry to validate quality/latency trade-offs and automatic rollback triggers if reranking quality or latency SLOs degrade beyond thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API accepts a 'vector_width' field for new embedding writes with clear server-side fallback semantics. 2) Indexer supports dual-width entries (primary width + fallback projection) during backfill window. 3) Client SDKs implement negotiation: negotiate width or opt-in to server-side projection with explicit warning. 4) Canary rollout process documented and automated (canary thresholds for recall@k, avg latency, and storage growth). 5) No customer-visible 5xx errors related to width changes during rollout. 6) Migration playbook with estimated time/cost published to SEs and CS.
implementation_overview: Phase A: Contract + SDK handshake (2 weeks) - extend embeddings API with optional 'vector_width' and 'accept_projection' flags; update spec and SDKs to perform a capability handshake at client initialization. Phase B: Dual-store indexing engine (3 weeks) - index supports storing canonical vector plus an optional compressed projection of the legacy width. Phase C: Online backfill scheduler (3 weeks) - prioritized reindex jobs per-tenant with rate limits and cost caps. Phase D: Canary + monitoring (2 weeks) - create dashboards for recall@k delta, p50/p95 token latency, and storage delta; automatic rollback on threshold breach. Phase E: Cleanup window (optional) - pruning legacy-width data after agreed retention window.
technical_tradeoffs: - Storing dual-width vectors increases storage and write IOPS; mitigation: compress projection using PQ/OPQ or 8-bit quantization for the fallback vector. - Server-side projection (projecting new width down to legacy width) is cheaper but may degrade reranking quality; prefer projection only as a transitional fallback with observable quality checks. - Synchronous negotiation increases client initialization latency slightly; to minimize pain, handshake cached at connection-level and optionally async for short-lived clients. - Online backfill will contend with regular indexing; rate-limited worker pools and tenant-level quotas required.
rollout_plan: 1) Spec + SDKs published internally and to canary customers. 2) Enable 'accept_projection' feature flag for non-critical tenants. 3) Run indexer in dual-mode (store both widths) for canary tenants and measure metrics for 2 weeks. 4) Trigger controlled backfill for high-priority tenants (SE-assisted). 5) Expand to broader set with automated scaling of backfill workers. 6) After retention window and customer confirmation, prune legacy-width vectors.
metrics_and_alerts: Primary: recall@10 delta between old and new widths (target delta <= 0.5% for production workloads), avg embed create latency (p50/p95), index storage delta per-tenant, backfill queue depth, success/error rates for embed write/read. Alerts: recall delta > 1% for more than 30m, backfill error rate > 2%, p95 embed latency increase > 50% relative to baseline.
backwards_compatibility_model: - New writes: clients specify 'vector_width' (optional). If absent, server uses tenant default. - Reads: server returns vector metadata including 'width' and 'projections_available'. - Legacy clients: if 'accept_projection' is true on tenant level, server will project to legacy width transparently; if false, legacy clients receive 422 with guidance. - SDKs: offer a warning-only path and a strict path. Warning-only path logs compatibility warnings to client telemetry but proceeds; strict path raises an explicit error.
client_impact_and_messaging: - SDKs must be updated to support handshake. Provide migration guide for: (a) toggling accept_projection, (b) validating reranking outcomes using sample prompt sets, and (c) enabling canary with subset of traffic. - Customer-facing messaging templates for SEs and CS: include expected storage change, expected cost, rollback plan, and estimated backfill duration per 1M vectors. - Provide a compatibility checker CLI that simulates projected quality loss from projection for a customer's sample dataset.
open_risks: 1) Projection quality might vary widely by model and dataset leading to surprises in reranking quality. Mitigation: require per-tenant small-sample validation and a holdback period. 2) Backfill heavy tenants could spike infra costs. Mitigation: tenant quotas and opt-in scheduling. 3) SDK adoption lag: old clients may hit 422s; mitigation: gradual opt-in and server-side projection for 90 days.
updates: 2025-09-10 Asha Patel: Ticket created after spike with SEs; prototype showed server-side projection with PQ had ~0.9% recall delta on our internal reranking benchmark.
2025-09-17 Diego Morales: Implemented API prototype adding 'vector_width' and 'accept_projection' flags; pushed draft SDK handshake to github (sdk-js PR 482).
2025-09-23 Emma Li (PM): Reviewed rollout plan; requested clear canary thresholds and customer comms; noted priority for enterprise tenants with dedicated Dedicated capacity.

2025-09-29 Diego Morales: Dual-store index design landed (runtimes PR 2618). Initial performance tests: write latency +12% p95, read p95 unchanged. Added compressed fallback projection using 8-bit quant + small PQ; storage delta ~+22% for canary tenant.

2025-10-05 Reliability team: Observability dashboard prototype live; recall@10 delta and backfill queue metrics added. Ran first 48h canary on internal test tenant — recall delta 0.45%, avg embed create latency +9%.
2025-10-07 Asha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require automated rollback on recall delta >1% for longer than 30 minutes. Preparing SE playbook and customer comms for next cycle.
2025-10-07 Diego Morales: Blocker identified — heavy backfill for tenant T-8793 caused storage indexer memory pressure; mitigation routes added (lower backfill concurrency & throttling).
notes: Related work: this ticket should coordinate with embedding-dim index lifecycle docs and the Dedicated capacity autoscaling initiative. Consider flagging for an infra cost review once we move beyond canary. Keep customers informed via SEs with precise cost estimates and optional assistance for backfill scheduling.
